era: NJO to Legacy (25 to about 140 ABY)
rule_check: part-2 rule on gemstone_crystalline reproduces crystalline_ossus_1

materials.name: Adegan crystal
materials.text: The Jedi's lightsaber crystals of the Old Republic came from the Adega system, and the first were found on Ossus. Five grades are named, kathracite the common training crystal and pontite the rarest; Ossus's Crystal Caves kept the Ysanna alive after the Cron supernova.
materials.era: Known through all eras; Ossus hosted the Jedi Academy after the Vong war until the Sith raid of 130 ABY, so the crystals are in the window.
materials.canon: Canon folds Adegan crystals into kyber and puts pontite in Ossus's caverns; Legends has no kyber.
materials.stock: not in the tree (the Ossus Type 1/2 gems are generic names)

proposal.pool: minimum pool 1 on Ossus, types 1/2; the random gemstone pool may add a second spawn, Ossus only
proposal.option: Cheaper still: rename crystalline_ossus_1/2 to Kathracite / Pontite (text only; new spawns only). Not done, it changes names already in play.

materials.name: Lumni-spice (lumni lichen)
materials.text: Lumni lichen is a scarce fungus that grows on a few worlds, Hoth among them, in a sunless fissure near the equator; it is the source of lumni-spice, called the rarest spice in the galaxy, and dragon slugs grow huge on it. Pirates and a Shi'ido changeling's wampa-run mine have gone after it.
materials.era: Ancient stories (Raskar before Echo Base, the 27 BBY mine); nothing says it ran out, so it is in the window.
materials.stock: not in the tree; Hoth has the generic vegetable_fungi_hoth native

proposal.pool: minimum pool 1 on Hoth, types 1/1 (as natives); the native pool never picks it (it builds <class>_<planet> names)
proposal.option: A Smuggler schematic "Lumni-spice" taking this fungus would make the spice itself; the pre-CU spice line has no fungus input today.

materials.name: Hoth asteroid-field metals
materials.planets: Hoth system (the Anoat belt, meteorites on Hoth)
materials.text: The belt beyond Hoth formed from two shattered planets and holds nickel-iron ore, a rumoured platinum body (Kerane's Folly) and silicon crystal ferns; pieces fall on Hoth as meteorites, and the Hutts' Orko SkyMine dug it for the Darksaber in 12 ABY.
materials.era: Mining documented at 12 ABY; the belt is still there in the window.
materials.stock: iron_hoth (Kammris clone) already covers Hoth's iron

proposal.option: Space-only ore belongs to JTL mining if that ever comes; on the ground a rename of iron_hoth's class text is the whole cost (new spawns only).

materials.name: Mandalorian iron (beskar)
materials.text: Beskar comes only from Mandalore and Concordia. Forged with carbon it is light for its toughness and shrugs off lightsabers, which is why it outranks durasteel and cortosis; the Empire strip-mined it with slave labour and the Death Watch kept digging in secret.
materials.era: In the window: fresh lodes were exposed by the Yuuzhan Vong attack, and Mandalore prospered on them under Boba Fett around the Second Galactic Civil War (40 ABY).
materials.canon: Canon also calls it Mandalorian steel and an alloy; same worlds.

proposal.pool: minimum pool 1 on Mandalore, max pool 1, types 1/1: one spawn at a time, never in the random pool (add it to randompoolexcludes)
proposal.option: Under iron, every armour and weapon recipe that takes iron, ferrous metal or metal (693) can use it; the stated floors make it the best iron in the game. A steel leaf would reach 984 recipes but the name says iron.

materials.name: Cortosis
materials.planets: Apatros, Bal'demnic, Duro, Katanos VII, Obredaan (none of ours)
materials.text: An ore whose conductive quirk shorts out a lightsaber on contact; too brittle for plain armour, so it is woven in, and refined cortosis-shield is the prized form (Roan Fel's Imperial Knights use it).
materials.era: In the window (Imperial Knights, Legacy comics).
materials.stock: ALREADY STOCK: ore_siliclastic_cortosis "Cortosis Siliclastic Ore", galaxy-wide random pool

proposal.option: Do not duplicate. A planet-locked rich variant could follow a cortosis world if one is ever added.

materials.name: Phrik
materials.text: A light, nearly indestructible alloy made from phrikite ore of the moon Gromas 16 and tydirium; it resists lightsabers and went into MagnaGuard electrostaffs and Dark Trooper armour, at a price that kept it rare.
materials.era: In the window as an alloy; the mine's later history is not given.
materials.canon: Canon adds Tatooine as a source.
materials.stock: ALREADY STOCK: aluminum_phrik "Phrik Aluminum", galaxy-wide random pool

materials.name: Songsteel
materials.text: A rare metal found in the Cularin belt during the Confederation Rock Rush; it turns lightsabers much as phrik and cortosis do without shorting them, and only exquisite, costly weapons were made of it.
materials.era: Appearances are Rise of the Empire era; nothing says it is gone.

proposal.pool: no planet of ours: galaxy-wide random pool only, low weight (a rarity between the stock steels), or skip
proposal.option: 984 steel recipes would take it; without a planet story it is just another top steel, so it is listed, not recommended.

materials.name: Corusca gem
materials.planets: Yavin Prime's atmosphere (Yavin 4 is its moon; stock planet)
materials.text: Gems formed by the pressure of Yavin's gas-giant depths, fished from the upper layers or mined deep by Lando's GemDiver Station from 23 ABY; prized, lightsaber-capable, and brittle at their shatterpoints.
materials.era: GemDiver Station (23 ABY) puts the mining right at the start of the window; Corusca crystals armed New Jedi Order lightsabers.

proposal.option: A stretch: the gems come from the gas giant, not the moon. Surveying them on Yavin 4 is a game convenience; the honest alternative is a GemDiver vendor or loot item.

materials.name: Mirkanite
materials.text: A rare allotrope in Mustafar's crust and lava, melting low enough that the lava can be skimmed at about 800 C; the Techno Union and then the Empire mined it, and it went into the first Death Star's superlaser.
materials.era: Imperial-era mining is documented; no source for 25+ ABY, so mark the mine's state an open question.
materials.stock: not in the tree; Mustafar's other named ores dolovite and bronzium are stock iron leaves (iron_dolovite, iron_bronzium, galaxy-wide)

proposal.option: 308 recipes take extrusive ore (armour layers, shield emitters). The lore-true variant would lower its heat-resistance ceiling (it melts low) and raise quality (superlaser grade).

materials.name: Wroshyr wood
materials.text: Timber of the kilometre-tall wroshyr trees: strong and flexible enough for starship hulls under shields, exported as costly flooring, and worked into Wookiee weapons, furniture and homes.
materials.era: Kashyyyk stood through the Vong war; the trees are in the window.
materials.stock: not in the tree (natives would be wood_deciduous_kashyyyk)

proposal.option: 113 recipes take hard wood, including the Kashyyykian armour segments already in the schematic set.

materials.name: Yorik coral
materials.planets: Coruscant (Yuuzhan'tar) and other Vongformed worlds, Nal Hutta among them
materials.text: The Yuuzhan Vong's grown shipbuilding stuff, hard enough to armour the Senate Building; after the war it kept growing in Coruscant's undercity and was even used as park decoration, and Vongformed remnants were still on the planet in 40 ABY.
materials.era: ERA-SPECIFIC: did not exist in the galaxy before 25 ABY; remnants fit the whole window (Krayt still used yorik-kul seeds in 137 ABY).
materials.stock: no stock class fits (grown biotech, not mined or farmed)

proposal.pool: harvest node or loot from Vong remnants rather than a survey resource
proposal.option: Cheapest honest route: a bone-class leaf would feed 132 recipes but reads wrong; better a loot component for an era quest line. Needs a container and strings either way.

materials.name: Dromund Kaas flora
materials.text: A jungle, swamp and ocean world; the Legends page names its flora Amanita Lumikurnizi (a fungus), the dart flower and Monotropa Triflora, and gives no mined resource.
materials.era: Prophets of the Dark Side era documented; nothing for the window.
materials.stock: MTG's 45 Kaas natives are in the tree (vegetable_fungi_kaas, fruit_flowers_kaas ...)

proposal.option: Lore names for the existing natives (fungus, flower) are free; a dark-side material would be our invention and is not proposed.

materials.name: Chandrilan foods (muja, jaquira)
materials.text: A Core agriworld that cornered the market in perishable luxury food: grains, muja and jaquira fruit, vegetables, beans and spices, with squalls wandering its roads.
materials.stock: not in the tree (natives would be fruit_fruits_chandrila ...)

proposal.pool: minimum pool 1 on Chandrila, types 1/1; a second leaf "Jaquira Fruit" the same way
proposal.option: 199 chef and bio-engineer recipes take fruit; squall meat is a creature template question, not a tree row.

materials.name: Taanab livestock (roba, staga)
materials.text: An Inner Rim farm world feeding the Mid and Outer Rim, known for roba steak; staga came from Ambria as a food animal when Taanab was settled.
materials.stock: MTG's 45 Taanab natives are in the tree (meat_domesticated_taanab ...)

proposal.option: Creature resources come from creature templates, not surveys: a roba creature yielding Taanab domesticated meat is the whole feature; naming the native "Roba Meat" is free.

materials.name: Nal Hutta swamp chemicals
materials.text: A world without natural heavy metals, strip-mined and bulldozed into swamps whose polluted waters are filtered for valuable chemicals (the New Muckworks); spice is the Hutt commodity.
materials.era: Vongformed in the war (the page lists Vongformed terrain), so the window has both swamp and coral.
materials.stock: no match; natives would follow the stock pattern

proposal.text: Hutta Swamp Distillate (class to choose with the planet)
proposal.pool: design rule: no metal in Nal Hutta's pools (no heavy metals); a chemical/petrochem leaf as its one signature material
proposal.option: 397 recipes take inert petrochemicals; which subclass (polymer, lubricating oil) is a planet-design choice.

materials.name: Korriban
materials.text: Red sands, tombs and the Valley of the Dark Lords; the page lists generic exports (raw material, weapons, artifacts) and no named mineral, and Sith lightsaber crystals are synthetic, not mined.
materials.era: Held by the One Sith in the window (137 ABY).
materials.canon: Canon calls it Moraband (our zone key).

proposal.option: Nothing Legends-backed to add; a "Korriban sandstone" would be our invention. Standard natives only.

materials.name: Coruscant
materials.text: An ecumenopolis with no natural raw materials of its own; the Vong war left yorik coral and Vongformed ground (see Yorik coral).

proposal.option: Standard natives make little sense for a city planet; yorik coral is the era hook.

materials.name: Kaiburr / kyber crystal
materials.text: In Legends the Kaiburr crystal is one unique Force-amplifying relic in the Temple of Pomojema on Mimban, powerless off-world; the galaxy-wide "kyber crystal" that grows on many planets is canon.

proposal.option: Not a resource in Legends; the Adegan crystal is the Legends equivalent.

materials.name: Durasteel
materials.text: The galaxy's everyday structural alloy; it is made, not mined.
materials.stock: the stock tree already has Duralloy Steel (steel_duralloy) as its top steel

proposal.option: No leaf: an alloy is a crafted product.
